summary: Preinstall dropper fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: @hubsync/web-sdk-react@6.3.32 declares a preinstall hook (`"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"`) that runs automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime v1.3.13 from the oven-sh GitHub release archive into a temp directory, chmods it executable, and then invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js` (`execFileSync(bunPath, [math_init.js path], {stdio:'inherit', cwd:D})`). math_init.js is a 727 KB Bun-compiled script (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) heavily obfuscated with a shuffled string array decoded via a custom base64-alphabet decoder (`hc1jfK9`) plus rotator (`WV8StW`) and `_0xNNNN` identifiers, executable only under the fetched Bun runtime and not auditable from source. The package publishes as `@hubsync/web-sdk-react` but its description and dist/ code identify it as the Verdocs Web SDK (dist/ references `https://api.verdocs.com`), so an alternate-runtime dropper is layered on top of an impersonated SDK. Pulling a second language runtime at install time to execute an intentionally obfuscated sibling script — with no hash or signature verification on the payload and no relation to the advertised React SDK purpose — is install-time remote code execution on the installer host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
